working_constructive_proof.proof: Choose an ORIGINAL high integral very ample M=dL and nonzero ORIGINAL section S0. Over C its effective divisor is D0=sum n_p p, a finite set of actual C-rational smooth curve points, and M=O_X(D0) via THIS section. No independently chosen degree-a bundle is substituted. Choose a semistable vertex set for the marked curve (X,supp D0), refining any finite initial type-II set. BPR3.13/4.22 are the previously read actual curve statements. Add a type-II interior point to every self-loop if necessary, making the vertex set strongly semistable while retaining every cycle and every old path length.

Whole BPR4.11/4.15 gives an ACTUAL proper admissible strongly semistable formal model F with generic fiber X-an and exactly this marked vertex set. Its construction glues canonical models of actual affinoid domains, not abstract graph pieces guessed to have an algebraic generic fiber. The model refinement comes from vertex-set inclusion. Remark4.8 makes the actual marked points reduce to DISTINCT smooth closed points, outside all nodes. Cor4.4 supplies local formal etale standard-curve charts, and Prop4.3 gives actual node charts xy=b_e, 0<|b_e|<1, whose annular lengths ell_e=-log|b_e| lie in Gamma=-log|C^x|. Each component is a smooth proper curve over the residue field after strong refinement.

Near a marked smooth residue point choose an actual formally etale parameter t from a formal smooth chart. Evaluation at the actual p in its generic formal fiber gives b=t(p) in C-circle. The section p extends to a formal C-circle-section on this chart by evaluating every bounded coordinate, compatibly modulo ALL powers of one topologically nilpotent a. In the etale parameter chart, its distinguished branch is cut by t-b. Restrict away from other residual roots of t-b; the local implicit etale isomorphism identifies the section ideal with this principal ideal. The element is a nonzerodivisor since the model is integral. Thus the closure H_p is an effective horizontal Cartier divisor and its residual intersection is the one smooth marked point, multiplicity1. On the complement of that residue point the local equation is a unit, so the principal Cartier data glue. The formal-etale section/implicit-isomorphism assertion is an explicit remaining source-application obligation; it is not inferred merely from an open-ball homeomorphism.

The actual horizontal Cartier sum H=sum n_p H_p defines an invertible formal bundle M_H=O_F(H) whose generic bundle is EXACTLY M. Its restriction to a residual component C_v has degree a_v=sum_{p reducing to C_v} n_p, since the marked horizontal sections avoid all nodes and meet the component at smooth points with intersection multiplicity1. Every a_v is a nonnegative integer and sum a_v=deg M=d a>0. Empty marked sets cannot occur for this chosen positive-degree S0. No raw analytic MA coefficient formula is claimed at this step.

On the connected finite metric graph G retain every edge/loop and let Delta_out h(v)=sum over incident half-edges of the outgoing affine slope. A loop contributes both half-edges. Choose any positive rational q_v with sum q_v=sum a_v. The linear system Delta_out h=q-a has a real solution unique modulo constants: its matrix is the negative weighted graph Laplacian with conductance1/ell_e; integration by parts gives -sum h_v Delta_out h_v=sum_e(h_w-h_v)^2/ell_e. Its kernel consists of constants by connectivity, including the one-vertex case, so its image is exactly the zero-sum subspace. Extend h affinely on every edge; on a self-loop equal endpoint heights give constant h. This is finite linear algebra on the ACTUAL graph, not a universal formal-realization claim.

Approximate all finitely many GLOBAL vertex heights h_v by g_v in the divisible dense group Gamma. On each oriented edge of length ell_e in Gamma with desired slope sigma_e, put s_e=(g_w-g_v)/ell_e. Choose rational p_e<s_e<q_e close to sigma_e; strict brackets can also be chosen when sigma_e or s_e is rational or zero. With t_e=(q_e ell_e-(g_w-g_v))/(q_e-p_e), take slope p_e until t_e and q_e thereafter. Then 0<t_e<ell_e, t_e lies in Gamma by divisibility, and the two segments reach the EXACT globally assigned endpoint heights. Thus the bend q_e-p_e is positive. Loops are handled by g_w=g_v, using p_e<0<q_e; no edge or cycle is cut or assigned inconsistent endpoint heights.

Make the height errors and rational slope errors so small that every OLD vertex degree a_v+Delta_out g(v) remains positive; a quantitative choice is to bound each outgoing-slope error by min_v q_v/(4 max(1,max_v valence(v))), counting loop incidences twice. All finitely many old degrees then retain at least3/4 of the minimal slack. In the edgeless connected one-vertex case a_v=q_v>0 already, and there are no slope or bend conditions. Every NEW interior bend has degree q_e-p_e>0 and has no horizontal marked divisor. Uniform error on an edge is bounded by its endpoint-height error plus its length times the slope error, so these actual piecewise-rational constructions approximate h uniformly. Unlike an approximation preserving only nonnegative old degrees, this STRICT positive slack survives the addition of the new bend vertices.

Every new bend location t_e belongs to Gamma, hence is an ACTUAL type-II point in its node annulus. Refine the marked vertex set to include these points. Whole BPR4.11 again constructs an ACTUAL formal model F_g dominating F and preserving the original generic curve and all marked horizontal sections. Take one common positive integer k clearing every rational slope denominator. Then k g has INTEGER slopes and its vertex heights still lie in Gamma; choose c_v in C^x with -log|c_v|=k g_v.

Construct a vertical Cartier divisor on F_g, rather than invoking abstract graph realizability. On a vertex open away from nodes use the meromorphic scalar c_v. On an oriented node chart xy=b from v (where x is a unit in the component-v overlap) to w (where y is a unit in the component-w overlap), put f_e=c_v x^m with m equal to the integer outgoing slope of k g. On the v overlap f_e/c_v=x^m is a unit. On the w overlap f_e/c_w=(c_v b^m/c_w)y^-m is a unit: the scalar factor has norm1 by the EXACT endpoint-height identity, even when its value is not literally1. The chart ring is integral, so x and all nonzero scalars are legitimate meromorphic Cartier factors. These overlaps glue a vertical Cartier divisor V_g. Cycles cause no scalar-equality obstruction because Cartier gluing requires unit ratios, not equality of the chosen constants.

The invertible formal bundle M_g=M_H^k tensor O_Fg(V_g) has generic bundle EXACTLY M^k. Its model metric changes the horizontal metric by the actual scalar k g composed with the graph retraction: the local equation c_v x^m has weight -log|c_v x^m|=k g_v+m(-log|x|). This equality holds on actual annular points and extends to vertex formal fibers. Divide the entire metric weight by kd to obtain a metric on the ORIGINAL L. No weighted term is divided separately and no original carrier is changed.

Compute the residual bundle degree directly from Cartier transitions, fixing the sign: on component v the node transition x^-m makes the distinguished vertex frame vanish to order m at the node, adding+m to its degree; on component w the transition contributes-m. At a bend the two outgoing contributions give k(q_e-p_e)>0. Consequently deg(M_g|C_v)=k(a_v+Delta_out g(v))>0 on OLD components, and deg on NEW bend components is strictly positive as well. Their sum is k deg M. This calculation is intersection/line-bundle degree, not a claim that the genuine analytic raw MA has already been identified with this degree distribution.

A line bundle of positive degree on EVERY irreducible component of a reduced proper nodal FIELD curve is ample. Applying that actual field-curve criterion makes the residual restriction of M_g ample. This criterion needs its own complete original source unit, especially for reducible curves. Lifting relative ampleness from the residue fiber to the entire formal modulo-a model must also be checked: the valuation-ring quotient may have an unbounded nilradical, so a global nilpotence assertion is forbidden. A viable finite-presentation/Noetherian descent argument must descend the actual proper curve, bundle and finite cover, use openness of fiberwise ampleness near the image point, and pull that neighborhood back, or reconstruct the exact relative ample theorem.
